app/content/marketing-composition.text:
# marketing-composition Specification

## Purpose

Render public pages as ordered semantic content within a shared shell and retain stable boundaries for source-backed review and maintenance.

## Requirements

### Requirement: Ordered semantic page content
Registered public content pages SHALL render their normalized ordered sections through the marketing content contract. Sections SHALL represent independently meaningful semantic regions with source-neutral authored fields rather than opaque whole-page payloads. Explicit utility-page exceptions SHALL remain bounded to their purpose.

#### Scenario: Render a multi-section public page
- **WHEN** an installed public content page is requested
- **THEN** its registered ordered sections render through their corresponding owners and visible authored copy comes from the page data

### Requirement: Shared shell and navigation
Header, menus and footer SHALL remain shared shell responsibilities using the same resolved layout data across desktop and compact presentations. Shell navigation SHALL distinguish registered internal destinations from external links and supported fragments.

#### Scenario: Compact shell navigation
- **WHEN** a public page changes to a compact viewport
- **THEN** its shared shell preserves the same destination meaning and layout data without becoming a page-specific duplicate

### Requirement: Stable semantic review boundaries
Independently reviewed composition regions SHALL retain stable semantic identities and review selectors. Content, shell and explicitly excluded regions SHALL have distinct comparison boundaries; exclusions SHALL NOT remove required production shell content.

#### Scenario: Review content with an excluded approved header
- **WHEN** a source-backed content comparison excludes an already approved shared header
- **THEN** content is compared within its declared boundary and the production header remains present and unchanged by that exclusion

### Requirement: Source fidelity and later reuse are distinct decisions
Source-backed composition SHALL preserve approved hierarchy, assets, content boundaries and independent cases. Combining cases or changing shared owners for later reuse SHALL require the applicable explicit systemization decision rather than being treated as a prerequisite for source fidelity.

#### Scenario: Similar independent source cases
- **WHEN** two independent approved source cases resemble one another
- **THEN** their distinct review boundaries remain until an explicit shared-owner decision authorizes consolidation

app/content/media-delivery.text:
# media-delivery Specification

## Purpose

Keep production media durable, accessible and responsive while preserving actual constituent assets and source-neutral rendering contracts.

## Requirements

### Requirement: Durable constituent assets
Production rendering SHALL use durable constituent assets rather than expiring design URLs or flattened captures of a reference composition. Supplied source assets SHALL preserve their intended bytes and role unless an explicit asset transformation is authorized.

#### Scenario: Expiring reference asset
- **WHEN** a reference supplies a temporary asset URL
- **THEN** production uses the durable approved asset rather than depending on the expiring URL

### Requirement: Source-neutral image delivery
Editorial media SHALL resolve into the supported frontend media contract with truthful dimensions and alternative text. Committed static raster media SHALL use the owning optimized-image defaults, responsive sizing and supported blur behavior; SVG media SHALL retain its appropriate vector treatment without invented blur data.

#### Scenario: Render provider and static media
- **WHEN** equivalent editorial media comes from a static source or a provider
- **THEN** each renders through the supported media owner with truthful dimensions, sizing and accessibility information

### Requirement: Alternative text follows purpose
Content media SHALL have appropriate authored alternative text. Empty alternative text SHALL be used only for genuinely decorative media; presentation assets SHALL NOT replace readable semantic content.

#### Scenario: Decorative and informative images
- **WHEN** a region contains decorative artwork and an informative image
- **THEN** decorative artwork avoids redundant announcements and the informative image exposes its meaningful alternative

### Requirement: Delivery cost follows evidence
Media loading SHALL follow its owner defaults. Preloading SHALL be reserved for a proven critical image. Any permitted local exception SHALL name its specific rule and rationale at the owning use and SHALL NOT authorize expiring production URLs or flattened reference captures.

#### Scenario: Add a local delivery exception
- **WHEN** a specific media use cannot follow an otherwise applicable default
- **THEN** its documented exception covers only that use and rule while the durable-asset constraints remain intact

app/content/source-resolution.text:
# source-resolution Specification

## Purpose

Keep marketing content source-neutral and predictable across static, guarded CMS-ready and explicitly activated authoritative CMS modes.

## Requirements

### Requirement: Explicit source modes
Static mode SHALL operate without a CMS runtime dependency. CMS-ready mode SHALL keep admin and API routes unavailable with static fallback authoritative. CMS-powered mode SHALL activate only after schema, service, seed, readback and parity gates succeed.

#### Scenario: Unconfigured CMS-ready project
- **WHEN** a CMS-ready project has not completed activation
- **THEN** guarded CMS entry points do not imply availability and public content continues through its permitted static fallback

### Requirement: One normalized frontend contract
Static and provider content SHALL resolve on the server into the same source-neutral page, site-layout and section contracts. Provider-specific records and metadata SHALL NOT require a second frontend layout implementation.

#### Scenario: Switch an approved page source
- **WHEN** a page moves from static content to an activated provider source
- **THEN** equivalent normalized content renders through the same frontend section and shell contracts

### Requirement: Preserve recovery data until verified activation
The static seed baseline and permitted recovery source SHALL remain available until successful provider readback and parity verification establish activation.

#### Scenario: Seed without successful readback
- **WHEN** provider seeding finishes but readback or parity fails
- **THEN** activation is incomplete and the permitted recovery baseline is retained

### Requirement: Authoritative failure is not silent fallback
After a source is authoritative, missing, unpublished, invalid or failed authoritative content SHALL follow its explicit unavailable/error behavior rather than silently substituting stale static content. Authentication SHALL protect guarded authoring boundaries.

#### Scenario: Unpublished authoritative document
- **WHEN** an activated authoritative page is unpublished or invalid
- **THEN** its public response follows authoritative unavailability instead of quietly displaying the old static document

app/data-lifecycle/action-behavior.text:
# action-behavior Specification

## Purpose

Make non-form state changes understandable, recoverable and safe across action groups. Form submissions remain owned by app/data-lifecycle/form-behavior and initial reads by app/data-lifecycle/loading-state-behavior.

## Requirements

### Requirement: One pending action owner
A non-form mutation SHALL reject duplicate starts synchronously, preserve the activated action's dimensions and accessible label, and expose pending feedback on that action alone. Conflicting sibling actions SHALL be unavailable without additional spinners until settlement. Settlement SHALL clear the pending identity and allow supported recovery.

#### Scenario: Rapid action group activation
- **WHEN** a user activates an action repeatedly and then activates a conflicting sibling while its request is delayed
- **THEN** one mutation starts, only the chosen action is busy, and the conflicting action cannot start

### Requirement: Feedback follows ownership and lifetime
An action result SHALL have one primary feedback channel matching its meaning: local recoverable failure, persistent usable-context notice, transient discrete outcome, or durable replacement instructions. Coexisting channels SHALL communicate distinct information without repeating the same result. Field validation and initial read failures SHALL remain with their separate owners.

#### Scenario: Recoverable mutation failure
- **WHEN** an action fails while surrounding content remains usable
- **THEN** one local accessible error explains recovery, retained values match the recovery copy, and retry follows the same pending guard

#### Scenario: Durable completion instructions
- **WHEN** successful completion requires instructions that remain useful after transient feedback disappears
- **THEN** those instructions remain in content rather than existing only in a notification

### Requirement: Outcome channels remain specific
Recoverable action failures SHALL remain beside the affected action. Successful saves and discrete completed actions SHALL use the shared transient outcome channel. Persistent service failure, expired access and read-only access SHALL explain unavailable actions as persistent context rather than masquerading as a local mutation result. Healthy pages SHALL NOT gain notices solely to demonstrate them.

#### Scenario: Persistent read-only access
- **WHEN** available content is read-only and its mutation controls are unavailable
- **THEN** persistent nearby context explains that limitation without presenting an invented failed mutation

### Requirement: Destructive intent and reversible optimism
Destructive or explicitly confirmation-required mutations SHALL require confirmation before execution. Optimistic presentation SHALL be reversible on returned or thrown failure and SHALL NOT leave a failed change presented as committed. Authorization SHALL be enforced again at execution.

#### Scenario: Failed optimistic update
- **WHEN** an optimistic mutation is rejected or throws
- **THEN** the prior visible state is restored, durable state is unchanged, and the user can recover in place

#### Scenario: Cancel destructive confirmation
- **WHEN** a user cancels the confirmation for a destructive change
- **THEN** the mutation does not execute

### Requirement: Single completion navigation
Successful mutation navigation SHALL occur once without a redundant refresh. Detail deletion SHALL leave the deleted destination through replacement navigation; collection completion SHALL follow its owning collection's refresh behavior.

#### Scenario: Delete an open detail
- **WHEN** confirmed deletion of the currently open entity succeeds
- **THEN** navigation replaces that detail once and does not refresh or revisit the deleted route as completion work

### Requirement: Active send cancellation remains available
Pending sends SHALL retain their initiating action owner and an active cancellable run SHALL keep its cancellation control available. Neighboring loading SHALL preserve independently editable drafts under the loading contract.

#### Scenario: Cancel an active run
- **WHEN** a run is active while another content region loads
- **THEN** the user can still invoke cancellation and edit any independent retained draft

app/data-lifecycle/form-behavior.text:
# form-behavior Specification

## Purpose

Provide a consistent, accessible submission and recovery contract for complete forms, verified against real client and server boundaries.

This is the submission side of the data-lifecycle family. Initial and region loading belong to [loading-state-behavior](../loading-state-behavior/spec.md).

## Requirements

### Requirement: Accessible field feedback
Forms SHALL connect labels, required state, descriptions and validation errors to their actual controls. Invalid values SHALL produce inline field feedback instead of browser warning bubbles or transient notifications.

#### Scenario: Invalid submission
- **WHEN** a user submits missing or invalid required values
- **THEN** invalid controls expose their errors accessibly and submission does not reach the server

#### Scenario: Narrow viewport
- **WHEN** the form and its errors are displayed on a narrow viewport
- **THEN** controls, feedback and submit actions remain usable without horizontal overflow

### Requirement: Native keyboard submission
Forms SHALL use native form semantics, logical keyboard order and visible focus, and support keyboard submission through the same lifecycle as the submit button.

#### Scenario: Keyboard submit
- **WHEN** a user activates the submit action with the keyboard
- **THEN** the form starts its normal validated submission exactly once

### Requirement: Single pending submission
A form SHALL reject duplicate starts synchronously, expose pending state on its submit action without losing its accessible label, and disable conflicting actions until the operation settles.

#### Scenario: Repeated submission while pending
- **WHEN** repeated submit events occur before a delayed request settles
- **THEN** only one request starts and the submit action is busy and unavailable

### Requirement: Server authority
The server SHALL independently validate and normalize submitted values and enforce applicable authorization before performing a mutation. Client validation SHALL NOT be sufficient authority.

#### Scenario: Client validation bypass
- **WHEN** invalid values are sent directly to a submission endpoint
- **THEN** the server rejects them without performing the requested mutation

#### Scenario: Organization authorization
- **WHEN** a submission names a membership outside the authenticated user's active memberships
- **THEN** the request is rejected without performing the requested mutation

### Requirement: Recoverable submission failure
Recoverable operational failures SHALL appear once beside the affected form action, preserve non-sensitive values, unlock submission and permit retry. Field-specific server errors SHALL be associated with their fields.

#### Scenario: Failed request and retry
- **WHEN** a request fails and the user retries
- **THEN** non-sensitive entered values remain, one local operational error is shown, and retry follows the same pending rules

### Requirement: Explicit success behavior
Forms SHALL communicate one unambiguous result and retain values unless their specified success behavior requires clearing or navigation.

#### Scenario: Successful form submission
- **WHEN** a valid submission succeeds
- **THEN** one truthful result identifies its outcome and values follow the form's specified retention, clearing or navigation behavior

### Requirement: Authentication form recovery
Login SHALL preserve email and clear the password after server rejection, show an inline operational error, and maintain server-owned authentication and safe continuation behavior.

#### Scenario: Rejected credentials
- **WHEN** the server rejects login credentials
- **THEN** the email remains, the password clears, an inline error appears, and the user can retry

#### Scenario: Successful login
- **WHEN** valid credentials resolve an active organization
- **THEN** the user is redirected once to the validated local continuation

#### Scenario: Organization selection
- **WHEN** valid credentials require an organization choice
- **THEN** login continues to organization selection with its safe continuation retained

#### Scenario: Unsafe continuation
- **WHEN** a successful login includes an external continuation URL
- **THEN** navigation stays on the application's safe local fallback

app/data-lifecycle/loading-state-behavio.text:
# loading-state-behavior Specification

## Purpose

Keep data-dependent regions understandable and usable while reading data, reserving appropriate space and providing clear completion or recovery. This is the read/presentation side of the data-lifecycle family; [form-behavior](../form-behavior/spec.md) owns form validation, pending submissions, submission feedback, retry, and success.

## Requirements

### Requirement: Preserve independent known content
Loading regions SHALL preserve known headings, descriptions, navigation, and independent controls with their existing copy, destinations, visibility, and keyboard behavior. Loading SHALL NOT unnecessarily replace them with placeholders.

#### Scenario: Known navigation while a region loads
- **WHEN** a region's data is delayed but a navigation destination is already known
- **THEN** the link remains visible, keyboard reachable, and navigable while the region loads

#### Scenario: Independent draft during loading
- **WHEN** a neighboring region or operation is pending without depending on an editable draft
- **THEN** the draft remains editable and survives the transition to ready content, while only dependent actions are gated

### Requirement: Dependency-scoped loading
Each independently fetched region SHALL own its loading state. Only unknown data and actions whose labels, destinations, visibility, or availability depend on that data SHALL be represented by loading placeholders or unavailable controls.

#### Scenario: Independent regions
- **WHEN** one region is delayed while another region has usable content
- **THEN** only the delayed region enters loading and the usable region stays available

#### Scenario: No content to load
- **WHEN** a region has no existing content to fetch, such as a new conversation without message history
- **THEN** it does not display placeholders implying that existing content is being retrieved

#### Scenario: Data-dependent action
- **WHEN** an action needs unresolved data or permissions to determine its destination or availability
- **THEN** it cannot execute until those dependencies resolve

### Requirement: Live and loading layout parity
Loading compositions SHALL preserve the ready layout's hierarchy, child order, repeated structures, spacing, alignment, responsive behavior, height, radii, reserved borders, typography, truncation, and semantic accents. Ready content SHALL replace its reserved region without unrelated layout changes.

#### Scenario: Repeated content and narrow layout
- **WHEN** a table, list, or detail region changes between loading and ready at desktop or narrow width
- **THEN** repeated rows, final borders, footers, wrapping, and always-present controls follow the same layout and fit the viewport

#### Scenario: Known and unknown sizing copy
- **WHEN** a placeholder needs hidden sizing content
- **THEN** known final copy is reused exactly and unknown copy uses realistic exemplars with equivalent length and wrapping

### Requirement: Inert visual placeholders
Visual loading placeholders SHALL be non-interactive, non-selectable, and unavailable as accessible actions. They SHALL preserve the established component presentation and SHALL NOT introduce duplicate focus stops, action handlers, or repeated announcements.

#### Scenario: Keyboard traversal during loading
- **WHEN** a user tabs through a loading composition
- **THEN** focus reaches real available controls and skips every visual placeholder

#### Scenario: Accessible loading feedback
- **WHEN** a region enters loading
- **THEN** a concise region-owned status communicates progress without announcing each placeholder or hiding independent usable controls

### Requirement: Readable reduced-motion loading
Loading meaning SHALL remain perceivable with reduced motion or animation fallback. Independent controls SHALL remain readable, focusable, and operable. Motion SHALL NOT gate semantic content or interaction.

#### Scenario: Reduced motion
- **WHEN** a user requests reduced motion while a region is loading
- **THEN** the region retains its reserved layout and loading meaning, and independent controls remain usable without requiring animation

### Requirement: Distinct region outcomes and recovery
Regions SHALL distinguish idle content awaiting initiation from active loading, and settle into ready, empty, unavailable, recoverably failed, or fatal-prerequisite content appropriate to the result. Region failures SHALL explain the affected content and offer retry when recovery is possible. Initial or region loading and failure SHALL NOT be represented as transient mutation feedback.

#### Scenario: Idle region
- **WHEN** a region is waiting for user initiation or a prerequisite before a read begins
- **THEN** it communicates its idle state without implying that a request is already loading

#### Scenario: Empty result
- **WHEN** a successful read returns no items
- **THEN** the region displays its empty result rather than continuing to load or claiming a request failed

#### Scenario: Recoverable read failure
- **WHEN** a region read fails recoverably
- **THEN** one local failure state explains the affected content, preserves independent content, and retry can reach ready content

#### Scenario: Unavailable prerequisite
- **WHEN** content cannot be read because a required capability or prerequisite is unavailable
- **THEN** the region explains that limitation without an indefinite placeholder or a misleading success result

### Requirement: Distinguish reading from submission
Initial and region loading SHALL remain distinct from a user-initiated pending action. Form submission lifecycle behavior SHALL follow the sibling form-behavior contract, without replacing the form or duplicating its pending/result feedback through region loading.

#### Scenario: Form submission alongside readable content
- **WHEN** a form submits while other content is already available
- **THEN** the submit action owns pending feedback under form-behavior and unrelated content is not replaced by loading placeholders

app/delivery/contact-delivery.text:
# contact-delivery Specification

## Purpose

Define truthful, private behavior for explicitly configured contact delivery.

## Requirements

### Requirement: Delivery is explicitly configured and server-owned
Delivery-enabled contact submissions SHALL normalize and validate on the server and pass applicable submission protection before delivery. Recipients and credentials SHALL be server-owned. Missing required configuration SHALL produce an unavailable result.

#### Scenario: Delivery configuration missing
- **WHEN** a delivery-enabled endpoint lacks required configuration
- **THEN** it reports unavailability without implying successful delivery

### Requirement: Recipient-independent message content
Configured recipients SHALL be trimmed and deduplicated outside message construction. The normalized message SHALL communicate source and contact details with the configured reply path, without embedding recipient-specific assumptions.

#### Scenario: Multiple configured recipients
- **WHEN** equivalent configured addresses include whitespace or duplicates
- **THEN** normalized unique recipients receive the same appropriate message content through the configured delivery boundary

### Requirement: Truthful private delivery outcomes
Delivery success SHALL reflect the configured provider outcome. Provider failure SHALL return a generic operational error without exposing credentials or provider internals. Logs SHALL omit personal message content, addresses, recipients, credentials and personal provider-response data. Form preservation, duplicate protection and retry SHALL follow `app/data-lifecycle/form-behavior`.

#### Scenario: Provider rejects delivery
- **WHEN** the delivery provider rejects a valid guarded submission
- **THEN** no delivery success is claimed and safe recoverable feedback retains form values as required

app/delivery/submission-protection.text:
# submission-protection Specification

## Purpose

Protect explicitly exposed submission boundaries through reusable server guards without inventing blanket dashboard policy or new abuse thresholds.

## Requirements

### Requirement: Apply guards at exposed boundaries
Public, externally delivered, attachment-bearing or explicitly abuse-sensitive submissions SHALL run their applicable server guards before downstream work. Ordinary authenticated dashboard mutations SHALL NOT gain blanket protection policy merely from this capability.

#### Scenario: Guarded public submission
- **WHEN** a public submission reaches its endpoint
- **THEN** applicable guards execute before delivery, persistence or other downstream effects

### Requirement: Honeypot responses remain neutral
A triggered honeypot SHALL perform no downstream work and SHALL return the guard's neutral outward result without revealing detection.

#### Scenario: Filled hidden field
- **WHEN** a submission populates the honeypot field
- **THEN** downstream work does not run and the response does not disclose bot detection

### Requirement: Server-owned attachment validation
Applicable file submissions SHALL validate authorization, type, size and required content checks on the server and normalize accepted files before downstream use. Client checks SHALL NOT replace those checks.

#### Scenario: Bypass client file validation
- **WHEN** a direct request supplies an unauthorized or invalid attachment
- **THEN** the server rejects it before downstream processing

### Requirement: Policy-owned throttling and private diagnostics
Cooldown and rate-limit behavior SHALL reuse established policy. A missing threshold SHALL require an explicit policy decision rather than an invented limit. Provider limits SHALL complement applicable application guards. Guard diagnostics SHALL NOT log personal submission content.

#### Scenario: Existing cooldown is active
- **WHEN** a guarded endpoint receives another submission inside its established cooldown
- **THEN** the existing policy determines the safe response without exposing personal content in diagnostics

app/domain/entity-presentation.text:
# entity-presentation Specification

## Purpose

Keep entity facts, identity, actions and collection meaning consistent across detail pages, collections, selectors and genuine tool presentations.

## Requirements

### Requirement: One consistent presentation vocabulary
The same entity SHALL present consistent identity, labels, fields, destinations, supported variants and commands across detail, collection, selector and tool surfaces. Provider data SHALL be adapted before presentation, and organization membership SHALL remain distinct from global identity under `app/identity/access-and-membership`.

#### Scenario: Entity appears in a selector and detail
- **WHEN** a user selects an entity and opens its detail
- **THEN** the visible identity and destination correspond to the same entity contract

### Requirement: Authorized recoverable lifecycle
Entity mutations SHALL follow server authorization and `app/data-lifecycle/action-behavior` for confirmation, reversible optimism and single completion navigation. Entity loading SHALL follow `app/data-lifecycle/loading-state-behavior`. An entity family SHALL implement only its actual product needs rather than imply unsupported operations.

#### Scenario: Failed entity update
- **WHEN** a server rejects a proposed entity update
- **THEN** the prior visible entity state is recoverable and the UI does not imply an unsupported or completed operation

### Requirement: Collection pagination and overview continuation differ
A complete collection SHALL expose its actual paging behavior. An overview continuation SHALL navigate to the owning collection rather than imitate loaded collection pagination.

#### Scenario: Continue from an overview
- **WHEN** a user activates an overview's continuation
- **THEN** it opens the owning collection and does not falsely claim the overview is the complete paginated dataset

### Requirement: Tool presentation corresponds to execution
An entity tool presentation SHALL exist only for a genuine supported typed tool path. It SHALL preserve the entity's presentation contract and SHALL NOT imply execution from a decorative or disconnected example.

#### Scenario: Present an entity tool result
- **WHEN** an entity tool result is shown as an executable interaction
- **THEN** it corresponds to the actual supported tool path and consistent entity identity

app/experience/content-hierarchy.text:
# content-hierarchy Specification

## Purpose

Make content grouping, context and emphasis understandable across application surfaces without freezing component APIs or prescribing a new button-variant policy.

## Requirements

### Requirement: Coherent grouping and surface meaning
Content SHALL be grouped by a coherent task or identity rather than putting every property in an independent surface. Persistent chrome, page content, cohesive cards and temporary floating content SHALL retain their distinct roles. Visual elevation SHALL NOT change semantic ownership.

#### Scenario: Present related record properties
- **WHEN** a detail presents multiple properties of one coherent record group
- **THEN** grouping communicates that relationship without introducing independent cards merely for spacing

### Requirement: Context is useful and not duplicated
Headings, labels and descriptions SHALL communicate distinct useful context. A group SHALL NOT repeat the same heading outside and inside its card. Permission, warning, count and other meaningful context SHALL remain present when redundant introductory copy is removed.

#### Scenario: Group with an external heading
- **WHEN** a card belongs to an already titled content section
- **THEN** the card does not repeat the section title and meaningful warnings or counts remain available

### Requirement: Shared alignment preserves usable controls
Related content headings, actions and surfaces SHALL follow their owning layout's shared gutters and alignment. Compact edge alignment SHALL preserve focus indicators, nonconflicting hit areas and control geometry rather than globally shrinking controls or adding compensating page offsets.

#### Scenario: Align a section action at a surface edge
- **WHEN** a compact action aligns with its neighboring content
- **THEN** its focus and activation area remain usable and do not overlap a neighboring control

### Requirement: Semantic color and identity remain legible
Foreground and fill roles SHALL remain distinct and readable on their actual composited surface, meeting applicable contrast requirements: 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 where applicable to large text or meaningful graphics. Decorative fills SHALL NOT be treated as meaningful graphics. Name-based identity colors SHALL NOT imply status, and static identity presentation SHALL NOT imply an active pressed state.

#### Scenario: Name-based avatar on a tinted surface
- **WHEN** an avatar uses a stable identity tint
- **THEN** its foreground remains readable and the tint does not falsely communicate status or interaction state

app/identity/access-and-membership.text:
# access-and-membership Specification

## Purpose

Preserve server-owned identity, organization and platform authorization across protected reads, changes and account lifecycle flows.

## Requirements

### Requirement: Server authorization at every protected boundary
Protected reads and mutations SHALL resolve the current session and required organization membership on the server. Only active authorized context SHALL grant access. Global identity, organization role and platform access SHALL remain distinct; organization administration SHALL NOT grant platform access and client visibility SHALL NOT authorize execution.

#### Scenario: Stale organization context
- **WHEN** a signed-in user submits a change for an organization in which they lack active membership
- **THEN** the server denies it without applying the change, even if the client displayed the action

### Requirement: Access denial remains usable
Protected UI receiving an unauthorized or forbidden outcome SHALL follow its supported authentication or denial route behavior rather than rendering blank content or remaining permanently loading.

#### Scenario: Access expires during a protected read
- **WHEN** a protected read returns an unauthorized or forbidden outcome
- **THEN** the UI follows its supported access-recovery or denial behavior without becoming blank or permanently loading

### Requirement: Safe continuations and explicit authentication methods
Authentication SHALL accept only safe supported continuation destinations. Optional sign-in methods SHALL remain unavailable until explicitly configured.

#### Scenario: Unsafe continuation
- **WHEN** a sign-in request supplies an unsupported external continuation
- **THEN** successful sign-in uses a safe supported destination

#### Scenario: Unconfigured optional method
- **WHEN** an optional sign-in method lacks configuration
- **THEN** it cannot establish a session through an implied fallback

### Requirement: Invitation acceptance is deliberate and bounded
Invitation reads SHALL NOT accept membership. Acceptance SHALL require an explicit mutation that validates the token, intended recipient, organization, expiry, revocation and prior use. Reinvitation SHALL invalidate the previous invitation as defined by the invitation owner.

#### Scenario: View and accept an invitation
- **WHEN** an invitation is viewed and later explicitly accepted
- **THEN** viewing makes no membership change and acceptance succeeds only after all invitation checks pass

#### Scenario: Reuse a replaced invitation
- **WHEN** a recipient attempts acceptance with a revoked, consumed, expired or replaced invitation
- **THEN** no membership is created from that invitation

### Requirement: Retain a verified sign-in identity
Account identity changes SHALL NOT remove the last verified sign-in identity needed to retain account access.

#### Scenario: Remove the last verified identity
- **WHEN** a user attempts to remove their only verified sign-in identity
- **THEN** the server rejects the removal and the existing access path remains usable

app/identity/private-file-access.text:
# private-file-access Specification

## Purpose

Keep private file access authorized and bounded through upload, reference resolution, replacement and deletion without exposing provider credentials.

## Requirements

### Requirement: Authorize file lifecycle boundaries
Private upload, metadata resolution, download, replacement and deletion SHALL enforce the owning resource's authorization and required metadata validation on the server. Possession of a client reference SHALL NOT substitute for access checks.

#### Scenario: Resolve another organization's file
- **WHEN** a user requests a private file outside their authorized resource context
- **THEN** neither file content nor private metadata is disclosed

### Requirement: Opaque references and bounded access
Private files SHALL use opaque application references and short-lived authorized signed access URLs. Provider secrets SHALL remain server-owned. Provider-specific storage records SHALL be resolved before reaching the frontend contract.

#### Scenario: Open an authorized private file
- **WHEN** an authorized user resolves a private file
- **THEN** the client receives only the permitted metadata and bounded access needed for that file

### Requirement: Explicit replacement and cleanup
File replacement and deletion SHALL follow the configured provider's explicit lifecycle, including applicable cleanup of superseded objects.

#### Scenario: Replace a private asset
- **WHEN** an authorized replacement completes
- **THEN** the resource points to the new asset and superseded-object cleanup follows its provider lifecycle without granting broader access

app/integration/api-transport.text:
# api-transport Specification

## Purpose

Make API outcomes consistent and testable while preserving server credential boundaries and frontend ownership of user-facing feedback.

## Requirements

### Requirement: Consistent request outcomes
Requests through a supported API client SHALL apply its shared base, headers, response parsing, cancellation and typed error contract. Callers SHALL receive typed data or errors rather than having to reinterpret inconsistent transport envelopes.

#### Scenario: Rejected API response
- **WHEN** an API response indicates failure
- **THEN** the caller receives the documented typed failure with enough safe context to choose its feedback

### Requirement: Replaceable transport with identical behavior
Tests and fixtures SHALL be able to inject transport and environment assumptions while exercising the same request wrappers used by application callers.

#### Scenario: Inject a failed transport
- **WHEN** a test substitutes a transport that rejects or returns an invalid response
- **THEN** the normal parsing, cancellation and typed-error boundary remains exercised

### Requirement: Secrets and feedback remain with their owners
Sensitive provider credentials SHALL remain on the server. Transport SHALL NOT own application-specific notifications or route behavior; the initiating UI SHALL translate safe outcomes into its lifecycle feedback.

#### Scenario: Provider failure reaches a client
- **WHEN** a server provider request fails
- **THEN** the client receives a safe failure without credentials and its initiating surface owns recovery feedback

app/interaction/keyboard-and-overlays.text:
# keyboard-and-overlays Specification

## Purpose

Keep controls and layered interactions operable through accessible names, native or documented keyboard behavior, predictable focus and consistent dismissal.

## Requirements

### Requirement: Accessible control ownership
Interactive controls SHALL retain their semantics, accessible names and visible focus. Native keyboard behavior SHALL be preserved where applicable; composite controls and scoped shortcuts SHALL use their documented interaction contract. Decorative wrappers SHALL NOT introduce focus stops or replace the real interaction owner.

#### Scenario: Keyboard operation with decoration
- **WHEN** a user traverses and activates a control decorated by animation or additional wrappers
- **THEN** its name, visible focus and keyboard behavior remain available on the real control without duplicate stops

### Requirement: Focus entry and return
Opening a focused blocking interaction SHALL place focus according to its owner contract. Closing it SHALL restore focus to an appropriate available initiator or documented recovery target. Nested overlays SHALL preserve topmost focus and dismissal ownership.

#### Scenario: Close a nested dialog
- **WHEN** the topmost dialog closes while its parent interaction remains open
- **THEN** focus returns to the appropriate parent control and the parent is not dismissed by the same action

### Requirement: Consistent pending dismissal lock
A mutable blocking flow SHALL apply one pending close lock to Escape, backdrop, explicit close and every other dismissal path. Recoverable failure SHALL unlock the same flow in place. Scroll locking and stacking SHALL remain consistent with active blocking layers.

#### Scenario: Dismiss during a delayed confirmed mutation
- **WHEN** a mutable dialog is pending and the user tries each supported close path
- **THEN** every path observes the same lock and no conflicting dismissal occurs

#### Scenario: Failure unlocks recovery
- **WHEN** the pending mutation fails recoverably
- **THEN** its error appears in place, dismissal unlocks consistently and retry remains available

### Requirement: Blocking and anchored interaction roles
Nonblocking anchored interactions SHALL preserve their documented anchor, keyboard navigation and dismissal behavior. Focused blocking interactions SHALL provide their documented modal behavior rather than imitating it through visual surface styling alone.

#### Scenario: Open an anchored menu
- **WHEN** a user opens an anchored menu with the keyboard
- **THEN** its owner supplies navigation and dismissal without introducing an unrelated blocking dialog or independent focus system

app/interaction/responsive-and-motion.text:
# responsive-and-motion Specification

## Purpose

Preserve essential content and user agency across viewport changes, motion preferences and animation fallback while avoiding unnecessary hidden expensive work.

## Requirements

### Requirement: Essential content survives responsive rendering
Primary copy, headings, navigation, essential controls and accessibility affordances SHALL remain available across supported viewport sizes and initial rendering. Responsive presentation SHALL NOT require a client-only breakpoint decision before essential content exists.

#### Scenario: Initial compact render
- **WHEN** a compact page initially renders before client breakpoint state resolves
- **THEN** primary content and essential accessible controls are already present and usable

### Requirement: Expensive hidden branches are bounded
Responsive implementations SHALL avoid mounting hidden expensive observers, media, canvas or duplicated decorative work when a deliberate branch can avoid that cost without withholding essential content. Lightweight layout and visibility changes SHALL preserve one coherent content model.

#### Scenario: Expensive desktop decoration on a phone
- **WHEN** the compact presentation excludes an expensive decorative branch
- **THEN** that work is not unnecessarily activated and essential content remains available

### Requirement: Motion does not gate agency
Reduced motion, motion-off and animation fallback SHALL leave content readable and real controls focusable and operable. Motion or conditional presence SHALL preserve control semantics, announcements and focus responsibilities with their interaction owners.

#### Scenario: Reduced motion during conditional content
- **WHEN** a user requests reduced motion while conditional content appears or disappears
- **THEN** the content settles readably and its controls remain usable without requiring animation completion

### Requirement: Motion has coherent ownership
Coordinated motion SHALL preserve a clear activation/progress owner and effect mapping without competing scheduling or reset behavior. Supported interruption, re-entry, resize and compact states SHALL settle into usable content according to the owning motion contract.

#### Scenario: Resize during playback
- **WHEN** the viewport changes or playback is interrupted
- **THEN** content and controls remain usable and competing animation/reset owners do not leave the surface stuck

app/navigation/document-metadata.text:
# document-metadata Specification

## Purpose

Provide consistent route-family titles, privacy directives and canonical/social identity from the same authoritative content used by the page.

## Requirements

### Requirement: Family title and indexing policy
Dashboard and authentication titles SHALL use route name followed by app name and private noindex/nofollow directives. Public titles SHALL use app name followed by route name, with the public home using app name alone. Internal development pages SHALL use route-first private metadata.

#### Scenario: Private and public page titles
- **WHEN** a user opens an authentication route and a public content route
- **THEN** each receives its family's title order and the private route is excluded from indexing and following

### Requirement: Canonical destination consistency
Canonical, robots, Open Graph and social metadata SHALL agree with the installed route identity and its indexing policy. Canonical destinations SHALL NOT inherit incidental query parameters or arbitrary CMS route identity. Utility metadata SHALL remain code-owned until explicitly migrated.

#### Scenario: Public route with incidental query parameters
- **WHEN** a public page is requested with tracking or unrelated query parameters
- **THEN** its canonical and social destination remain the installed canonical route

### Requirement: Metadata and body share authoritative content
Metadata and page body SHALL use the same resolved authoritative content read. Missing, invalid or unpublished authoritative content SHALL NOT produce metadata for a stale fallback page under `app/content/source-resolution`.

#### Scenario: Authoritative content changes during a request
- **WHEN** metadata and body resolve for one authoritative page response
- **THEN** they reflect the same resolved document rather than separate inconsistent reads

### Requirement: App identity is centrally derived
Page metadata SHALL derive shared app identity through the canonical metadata owner rather than hardcoding independent app names in individual pages.

#### Scenario: Shared app name changes
- **WHEN** the configured app identity changes
- **THEN** participating route metadata uses that identity without page-specific name replacements

app/navigation/route-identity.text:
# route-identity Specification

## Purpose

Keep installed destinations, semantic ancestry and contextual navigation consistent across public, authentication and dashboard route families.

## Requirements

### Requirement: Canonical installed destinations
Each installed product route SHALL have one canonical family identity and supported destination contract. Dynamic destinations SHALL use their typed parameters. Internal development routes SHALL remain distinct from product route identity. Omitted profile features SHALL NOT appear as installed destinations.

#### Scenario: Navigate to a dynamic detail
- **WHEN** navigation targets an installed detail with a resource identifier
- **THEN** all participating surfaces derive the same supported destination from its canonical identity and parameters

### Requirement: Semantic ancestry and consistent vocabulary
Navigation, breadcrumbs, page headings, loading labels and contextual commands SHALL use consistent destination vocabulary. Breadcrumbs SHALL contain navigable semantic ancestors rather than filesystem parents or arbitrary cross-links, and the current destination SHALL remain the page heading.

#### Scenario: Detail outside a filesystem-shaped hierarchy
- **WHEN** a detail's semantic parent differs from its directory ancestry
- **THEN** its trail uses the navigable semantic parent and does not invent intermediate breadcrumb destinations

### Requirement: Contextual actions follow the active surface
Surface-specific actions SHALL be available only while their owning surface is active and SHALL unregister on departure. Command search SHALL close before executing an action or navigation. Action visibility SHALL NOT replace server authorization under `app/identity/access-and-membership`.

#### Scenario: Leave a surface with contextual commands
- **WHEN** the active surface unmounts and another route opens
- **THEN** its former contextual commands are no longer offered

### Requirement: Route enrichment preserves identity
Dashboard navigation, domain grouping, capability visibility and presentation enrichment SHALL preserve the canonical route identity rather than create competing destination definitions.

#### Scenario: Destination appears in multiple navigation surfaces
- **WHEN** the same installed route is offered in sidebar and command navigation
- **THEN** both resolve to the same identity and destination despite their different presentation

app/ui-system/component-contracts.text:
# component-contracts Specification

## Purpose

Make supported shared UI behavior discoverable and faithful across runtime consumers, Storybook teaching and public catalogue/export projections.

## Requirements

### Requirement: Discoverable supported owner contract
Shared UI SHALL expose an intentional supported contract through its documented public owner and Storybook evidence. Source exports alone SHALL NOT imply public support. Consumers SHALL use the highest complete applicable owner without bypassing its semantics or focus behavior through styling.

#### Scenario: Choose a shared control
- **WHEN** a consumer needs behavior already covered by a complete supported owner
- **THEN** it uses that owner and its documented API rather than reconstructing the behavior from lower-level parts

### Requirement: Complete and neutral variant teaching
Public teaching SHALL cover each supported variant axis and meaningful interaction state with neutral reusable guidance. Adding or moving a public owner SHALL preserve useful existing teaching and migrate its consumers. Context-specific aliases SHALL NOT substitute for a genuinely reusable distinction.

#### Scenario: Add a supported owner variant
- **WHEN** an owner gains a public variant
- **THEN** its contract and teaching expose the complete supported choice and affected consumers remain consistent

### Requirement: Faithful public projections
Stories, catalogues and export previews SHALL project the same supported implementation and contract. Runtime code SHALL NOT depend on story or catalogue modules. Preview-specific shells and portals SHALL remain isolated, and deliberate reduced-profile omissions SHALL be represented accurately.

#### Scenario: Export a reduced-profile owner
- **WHEN** a generated profile supports fewer owner features
- **THEN** its catalogue and export teaching match those features without presenting unavailable variants

### Requirement: Native semantics remain mounted
Input and composite owners SHALL retain the real native or documented interaction owner responsible for value, keyboard, form and accessibility behavior. Decorative wrappers and specialized rendering SHALL NOT replace that owner with an inert imitation.

#### Scenario: Custom visual input presentation
- **WHEN** an input adds specialized visual presentation
- **THEN** the mounted interaction owner still supplies its supported value, keyboard, form and accessibility behavior

### Requirement: Stable public identity
Owner moves SHALL preserve public names unless an explicit migration changes them. A wrapper SHALL add distinct reusable behavior rather than rename an existing owner. Shared contract changes SHALL update teaching and consumers together.

#### Scenario: Move a shared component
- **WHEN** a supported owner changes source location without an API migration
- **THEN** consumers retain its public identity and teaching still resolves to the same supported behavior

template/demo-behavior.text:
# demo-behavior Specification

## Purpose

Keep the canonical template demonstrations truthful, resettable and isolated while allowing independently generated products to replace examples with real providers and persistence.

## Requirements

### Requirement: Resettable external-write-free fixtures
Fixture entities SHALL remain resettable and SHALL NOT perform external writes or imply durable production persistence.

#### Scenario: Reset a fixture session
- **WHEN** a fixture session is reset after entity changes
- **THEN** the fixture baseline returns without external provider writes

### Requirement: Guarded synthetic contact boundary
The public contact demo SHALL validate email and message on the server and terminate honeypot submissions neutrally before further work. It SHALL never deliver, persist or log submitted contact data and SHALL identify itself as a demo before submission.

#### Scenario: Honeypot hit
- **WHEN** a contact submission fills the hidden honeypot
- **THEN** the server returns the same neutral demo result without running subsequent validation or delivery work

#### Scenario: Public demo disclosure
- **WHEN** a user views or submits the contact form
- **THEN** its copy makes clear that it sends no email and stores no submission

### Requirement: Truthful support and contact demo results
Fixture contact and support forms SHALL retain their no-email behavior. Support success SHALL clear its subject and message and identify the saved fixture request. Contact demo success SHALL retain entered values and explicitly state that nothing was sent or stored.

#### Scenario: Support fixture saved
- **WHEN** a valid support submission succeeds
- **THEN** subject and message clear and one result identifies the saved fixture request without claiming email delivery

#### Scenario: Contact demo accepted
- **WHEN** a valid contact demo submission succeeds
- **THEN** entered values remain and the result explicitly states that nothing was sent or stored

### Requirement: Fixture authentication remains distinct
Fixture authentication SHALL remain non-durable and SHALL NOT imply a configured production provider. Unconfigured optional methods SHALL NOT establish a session through an implied provider fallback.

#### Scenario: Use fixture authentication
- **WHEN** a user signs in through the template fixture implementation
- **THEN** the example does not imply durable authentication or a configured production identity provider

### Requirement: Fixture storage remains distinct
Fixture behavior SHALL remain external-write-free and SHALL NOT masquerade as durable storage.

#### Scenario: No configured private storage adapter
- **WHEN** a template example lacks a configured private-file provider
- **THEN** its fixture does not perform external storage writes or imply durable storage

template/project-assembly.text:
# project-assembly Specification

## Purpose

Materialize independent projects from explicit positive ownership while preserving selected profile boundaries and excluding template-only machinery.

## Requirements

### Requirement: Positive output ownership
Generated files, scripts, dependencies and instructions SHALL have explicit assembly owners. Overlapping or missing ownership SHALL fail verification rather than silently select a copy. Source-bearing output SHALL remain file-backed rather than hidden in generated source strings.

#### Scenario: Conflicting output owners
- **WHEN** two assembly owners claim an incompatible destination
- **THEN** assembly verification rejects the conflict instead of producing an arbitrary project

### Requirement: Profiles preserve intentional boundaries
Selected profiles SHALL include their supported contracts and omit unsupported features, routes, dependencies, scripts and teaching. Full and thin-start differences SHALL remain intentional, with overrides limited to material boundaries rather than mirrored canonical source.

#### Scenario: Marketing-only assembly
- **WHEN** a marketing-only project is generated
- **THEN** its output includes applicable public-site contracts and verification without implying absent dashboard capabilities

### Requirement: Independent applicable policy and evidence
Generated projects SHALL receive independent stock OpenSpec integration, project-owned configuration, explicitly selected applicable app contracts and verification procedures/tests. Template contracts, change history, unrelated agent files and generator-only policy SHALL remain excluded. Installed-feature-dependent coverage SHALL match the generated surface.

#### Scenario: Modify a generated specification
- **WHEN** a generated project changes an applicable copied specification
- **THEN** it changes its own copy without mutating the template or another generated project

#### Scenario: Template contracts are excluded
- **WHEN** any supported profile is assembled
- **THEN** its maintained specs contain only explicitly selected app contracts, no template contracts or unprefixed legacy identities, and all app references resolve independently

#### Scenario: Production behavior replaces an example
- **WHEN** an independent app replaces demonstration entities, authentication, storage or contact handling with an authorized real implementation
- **THEN** its inherited app contracts permit real persistence and configured delivery without requiring resettable production entities or unconditional no-delivery behavior

### Requirement: Propagation follows proven ownership
Template changes SHALL propagate only through established assembly edges. Inventories and generated projections SHALL be regenerated from their owners. Instance work SHALL NOT acquire template machinery merely because it shares runtime paths or names.

#### Scenario: Update a canonical shared owner
- **WHEN** a canonical template owner changes
- **THEN** applicable generated outputs follow its established assembly edge while intentional profile omissions remain intact

### Requirement: Independent profile inheritance
Generated projects SHALL inherit the maintained app form contract and stock OpenSpec integration with tests for installed forms only, without template proposal history or references to omitted surfaces.

#### Scenario: Marketing project
- **WHEN** a marketing-only or thin-start project is assembled
- **THEN** contact verification is included and login/support test modules are omitted

#### Scenario: Application project
- **WHEN** an app-only project is assembled
- **THEN** login/support verification is included and contact implementation and test modules are omitted

### Requirement: Independent loading contract inheritance
Generated projects SHALL inherit the maintained app loading contract and verification procedure independently, without template change history. Executable pilot cases SHALL cover installed surfaces only and SHALL NOT retain references to omitted application areas.

#### Scenario: Profile-selected coverage
- **WHEN** a project is assembled with or without dashboard routes
- **THEN** its loading tests match its installed surfaces and omitted dashboard/authentication cases are not imported or executed
